newsitem.title: USA: AOL sees 2 qtr transition, Q3 EPS breakeven.
newsitem.headline: AOL sees 2 qtr transition, Q3 EPS breakeven.

text.p: America Online Inc said a broad set of restructuring steps and service pricing changes it announced earlier on Tuesday will hurt earnings during the next several quarters, but increase its competitivenes and ready it for the "next stage of growth."

In a conference call with analysts and reporters, America Online executives said the company expects to undergo a "two- quarter transition" during its current fiscal second quarter ending in December and the third quarter ending in March.
AOL said it expects revenues of $400 million and a net loss of about $0.32 a share during the December quarter.

AOL's Chief Financial Officer Len Leader said during the call that he expects the company's third fiscal quarter ending in March to result in revenues of $450 million and to be about breakeven in terms of earnings per share.
The company will return to profitablity in June, the fourth quarter of fiscal 1997, with earnings of about $0.05 per share and revenues of $500 million, the executive said.
Leader said the company expects to see earnings for the fiscal year ending in June 1998 in the range of $0.80 to $0.90 per share.
Also during the call, AOL Chairman and Chief Executive Steve Case said the company has begun to see a return to healthy new customer growth after a slowdown in subscribers during the summer season.
Case said the company expects to add 800,000 net new subscribers to its online and Internet access service during the current quarter ending in June.
As evidence of progress, he said that in the month of October alone, the company had added 250,000 net new subscribers.

Along with newly named chief executive of AOL's flagship online service Robert Pittman, Leader and other AOL officials stressed that revenues from sources other than subscriber fees have begun to ramp up and will become increasingly visisible in earnings results going forward.
The company said "other sources" of revenue will include online advertising, AOL brand merchandise sales and online transactions such as home shopping.
Leader said the company expects to report "other revenues" for the recently ended September quarter of "$35 to $40 million ... (and) closer to the high end of that range."
He said he expected that AOL would exit its fourth fiscal quarter ending June 1997 with other revenues of $80 million to $90 milllion, and $250 million for fiscal 1997 as a whole.
Pittman said the rising revenue from these other sources was a clear indication that the company has begun the transition from an online access company to a media company.
He emphasized that the company had entered what it considers a "mass market phase" of growth.

Leader also said he expects revenues to increase more than 50 percent during fiscal year 1998 over the 1997 fiscal year. He predicted AOL would see revenues from its core online business of roughly $1.5 billion and $250 million in other revenues.
Alex Brown analyst Steve Eskenazi said he believes that Leader was rounding up the figure for online services revenue for 1997, which is likely to be closer to $1.45 billion.
The analyst said he expects AOL to see $1.7 billion in revenues for 1997.
